Brook Trout, snakes and a rubber ducky.

So it's supposed to rain all week, so I got some trout fishing in this weekend. Yesterday I hit a combo of stocked lakes, got one Splake 17" and 5 brook trout about 14"(picture on the ground), I spent half the day on the Splake lake, got one right away around 10am, then a few bites, then the local JoHo(jehovahs witness) and his grandkid showed up and the bite instantly stopped once they got there and launched their boat. So I fucked off a mile up the road to a brook trout lake and got the 5 and lost just as many in about 2 hours, the brookie action was really hot, but they were all cookie cutter 14 inch clones. Still a good day took home a good 6 or 7 lbs of food probably.

Then today I hit up the creeks for native brookies, native brookies are smaller but more delicious and rewarding. I want to collect a shitload of small natives to smoke up dry so I can pack them in my backpack and take them hiking with me. Had a hell of a day on the creeks though, I just drove a couple hour loop down some dirt roads and fished the culverts and beaverponds that crossed the roads. Usually I might get one nice one maybe 2 and a few smalls but today the action was hot, got 4 nice ones 11" and 12" and the 3 smalls were hooked to bad to release but I caught 10 more just like them, they are around 8-9" which are decent creek fish and actually more the size I was looking for actually. The brookies in the creeks average 6-10 inches around here so catching 4 over 11" is a great night on the skinny water.

Saw a couple snakes took a picture of one, just garter snakes, they are all we get up here.

The Rubber Ducky is from about 15 years ago, the town held a raffle thing where everyone in town could buy a rubber ducky and they would release them all in a creek about 150+kms from lake superior, and the first couple ducks to make it to lake superior would win prizes, this duck made it about 20kms and I found it on the side of the creek, it has small punctures around it's head, probably a mink or a marten or otter or something tried to take a bite from it.

Anyways that's the gist of my weekend in the great outdoors, I'm ready for a few days of rain now.

Honestly I don't weigh 99% of my fish, I'll take a legnth but to me weight has never been more then a curiosity. an X inch fish is an X inch fish any day of the week it's never getting any smaller, but a fish can weigh more or less depending on pre or post spawn or eating a big meal. To me a longer fish is worth more then a fatter fish because a long fish can become a fat fish.

But I did read this comment last night and today I went to the tackle shelf at the hardware store with the intent on spending 40$, they had no tackle that I needed so I bought a digital fish scale, so I'll try to remember to weigh the bigger fish that I catch.

As estimates though the 17" Splake would have been about 3lbs and the 14" stocker brookies would be about a lb and a half.

The 4 bigger creekers would be around 1lb give or take and the smaller ones I have no clue
